\subsection{From the discretization to the continuous columnar operator}\label{sec:stageb}

The certificate of the preceding subsection is a statement about a finite matrix pencil. We now remove
the discretization: the same eigenvalue is enclosed for the continuous columnar operator, by a
argument of Plum's type for non-self-adjoint eigenvalue problems \cite[\S 9.3]{NPW19}, following \cite{LP04,WPN09}, whose two ingredients are a rigorous defect bound for an
approximate eigenfunction and a rigorous bound on the inverse of the shifted operator, the second
obtained from a certified block of the exact Stokes eigenbasis plus a-priori estimates on its
complement. Every constant below is an outward-rounded interval quantity; the computations that
produce them are described in the supplementary material and summarized in
Section~\ref{sec:stageb-arith}.

\medskip\noindent \emph{The operator.} Let $r_w := 0.027546\cos(\pi/400)$, let
$D_{r_w} \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be the open disc of that radius, and let
$Q := D_{r_w}\times(\mathbb{R}/(2\pi/k)\mathbb{Z})$ be the periodic cylinder, $k = 2000$,
$\nu = \sn{5}{-4}$. Let $\Omega(s)$ and $W(s)$ be the degree-30 polynomials in $s = (r/r_{\max})^2$
with exactly rational coefficients of the preceding subsection, $r_{\max} = 0.0275462274972771$, and
let the base flow be $U = r\,\Omega\, e_\theta + W e_z$. Perturbations are taken in the single Fourier
mode
\[
   u(r)\,e^{i(m\theta + kz) - i\omega t}, \qquad m = 1,
\]
so that the growth rate is $\operatorname{Im}\omega$. Let $H = H_{m,k}$ be the closure, in
$L^2(Q)^3$, of the divergence-free fields of that mode which are compactly supported in $D_{r_w}$;
equivalently, $H$ is the space of $u \in (L^2((0,r_w), r\,dr))^3$ with
$\operatorname{div}_{m,k} u = 0$ and $u_r(r_w) = 0$. Let $S$ be the self-adjoint operator of the
Dirichlet form on that space (Section~\ref{sec:stageb-chain}, step 1), and let
\[
   T u := P_H\!\left(a\,u + C u\right), \quad a = m\Omega + kW, \quad
   C u = \bigl(2i\Omega u_\theta,\; -i(2\Omega + r\Omega')u_r,\; -i W' u_r\bigr),
\]
with $P_H$ the Leray projection of the mode. The columnar operator is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stageb-A}
   A := -iS + T \quad\text{on } D(A) = D(S) \subset H,
\end{equation}
in units $\nu = k = 1$: that is, the physical operator divided by $\nu k^2 = 2000\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$,
and Stokes eigenvalues by $k^2$. Lengths are then measured in units of $1/k$, so that in every
formula written in these units --- steps 11 and 12 below, and the supplement throughout --- the wall
of $Q$ sits at radius $X = k r_w = 55.090300832967$, not at $r_w$; the physical radius $r_w$ appears
only in the description of the geometry and in the argument of the field polynomials.
Equation~\eqref{eq:stageb-A} is the primitive-variable system of the
preceding subsection with the pressure eliminated by $P_H$; the base flow has $U_r \equiv 0$, so $T$
is a bounded multiplication operator and not a differential one.

\medskip\noindent The theorem is posed on the cylinder of radius $r_w$, which is the wall of the
certified Stokes spectrum and of every rigorous computation below. Two bookkeeping facts are
hypotheses of the theorem rather than remarks.

\begin{itemize}
\item[(G1)] $r_w = 0.027546\cos(\pi/400)$, so $X := k r_w = 55.090300832967$. The field polynomials are
polynomials in $s = (r/r_{\max})^2$ with $r_{\max} = 0.0275462274972771$, a radius exceeding
$0.027546$ by $\sn{8.3}{-6}$ relative. The two radii play different roles and are not interchanged:
$r_w$ is the boundary of $Q$, $r_{\max}$ is a coefficient inside the polynomial field, and the field
is evaluated on $0 \le r \le r_w$. In particular the continuous problem enclosed here and the
collocation pencil of the preceding subsection are posed on cylinders whose radii differ by
$\sn{8.3}{-6}$ relative, so the agreement of the two eigenvalues to $\sn{5.0}{-9}$, quoted below, is
a convergence check across two discretizations and two radii, not a certificate.
\item[(G2)] The certified Stokes eigenvalue data are used in two files, one covering
$\lambda/k^2 \le \sn{4.8}{4}$ (its 7682 entries are the block of step 5) and one covering
$\lambda/k^2 \le \sn{6.97}{5}$; their first 7682 eigenvalue brackets are bit-identical, which is
verified at the head of the one run that reads both, the rectangle of step 10. The three eigenvalues
quoted in step 4, $\lambda_M$, $\lambda_{M+1}$ and $\lambda_{N+1}$, are taken from the larger file.
\end{itemize}

\medskip\noindent \textbf{Theorem 2 (the continuous columnar eigenvalue).}\label{thm:stageb}
\emph{Assume} (G1), (G2) \emph{and the arithmetic assumptions} (A1)--(A3) \emph{of
Section~\ref{sec:stageb-arith}. Let $M = 7682$, let $P$ be the spectral projection of $S$ on its first
$M$ eigenfunctions, let $w \in \operatorname{range}P$ be the stored Galerkin eigenvector of $PAP$,
normalized so that $\bigl|\,\|w\|^2 - 1\,\bigr| \le \sn{3}{-16}$, and}
\[
   \mu = -17.525873540058 + 25.425171859977\,i \quad (\text{units } \nu k^2)
       = -\sn{3.5051747}{4} + \sn{5.0850344}{4}\,i \ \ \mathrm{s}^{-1}
\]
\emph{its Galerkin eigenvalue. Then, with the certified constants}
\[
   K \le 2.7632556, \qquad \delta \le \sn{8.017048}{-3}, \qquad
   \beta := 4K^2\delta \le 0.2448593 < 1,
\]
\emph{the operator $A$ of \eqref{eq:stageb-A} has an eigenvalue $\omega$ with eigenfunction
$u \in D(S)$ normalized by $\langle u, w\rangle = \|w\|^2$ such that}
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stageb-encl}
   \bigl(|\omega - \mu|^2 + \|u - w\|^2\bigr)^{1/2} \le \rho := \frac{2K\delta}{1 + \sqrt{1-\beta}}
   \le \sn{2.370604}{-2} \quad (\text{units } \nu k^2; \ 47.42\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}),
\end{equation}
\emph{and $(\omega, u)$ is the only such pair in that ball. In particular}
\[
   \operatorname{Im}\omega \ \ge\ \sn{5.080293}{4}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}
   \quad (25.4014658 \text{ in units } \nu k^2) \ >\ 0 :
\]
\emph{the continuous columnar operator is unstable.} In collapse units, with the fitted
$T = 0.0022865$ and $T - t = \sn{2.4478}{-5}$ on the x144 state, the certified growth rate is
$1.2435 \pm 0.0051$ in units of $(T-t)^{-1}$, the uncertainty being the 0.41 percent that Remark 2 attaches to every collapse-unit quantity on this state.

\medskip\noindent \emph{What is claimed and what is not.} The theorem asserts the existence of an
eigenpair in the ball \eqref{eq:stageb-encl} and the local uniqueness of that \emph{pair}. It does not
assert that $\omega$ is the only eigenvalue of $A$ in the disc $|z - \mu| \le \rho$: an eigenvalue
exclosure is a different statement, requiring a certified lower bound on a second auxiliary
eigenvalue, and we do not claim it. Nor do we claim that $\omega$ is algebraically or geometrically
simple, or that it is the most unstable eigenvalue of $A$. The scope of the object is equally
important. The field is the explicit rational polynomial pair $(\Omega, W)$, which differs from the
grid column it was fitted to by $\sn{1.4}{-3}$ relative and whose first derivative is wrong by up to a
factor two at the swirl maximum; the operator is a parallel-flow columnar model carrying an artificial
no-slip wall at $r_w \approx 2R$, where the physical column has none; and the statement is about that
operator alone. Nothing here bears on the front itself, on the two-dimensional collapse, whose
operator has no isolated eigenvalue to enclose, or on regularity for the three-dimensional
Navier-Stokes equations.

\medskip\noindent \emph{How much the artificial wall matters.} The wall is the one feature of the
model with no counterpart in the column, so we measured its effect directly, by re-running the
collocation solver of the preceding subsection on the same field ($z = 0.00201$ of the x144 state,
degree-30 polynomials, $m = 1$, $k = 2000$, $\nu = \sn{5}{-4}$, $N = 150$) with the wall moved:

\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lllll}
wall radius & $1.5R$ & $2.0R$ & $2.5R$ & $3.0R$\\[2pt]
leading $\operatorname{Im}\omega$ (s$^{-1}$) & $\sn{5.0377}{4}$ & $\sn{5.0850}{4}$
  & $\sn{5.0543}{4}$ & $\sn{5.0597}{4}$\\
mode centre & $1.357R$ & $1.356R$ & $1.358R$ & $1.355R$\\
mode support & $[1.287, 1.409]R$ & $[1.283, 1.407]R$ & $[1.284, 1.416]R$ & $[1.292, 1.404]R$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent Doubling the wall radius moves the growth rate by 0.93 percent, and in every case the
eigenfunction is centred at $1.36R$ with support ending near $1.41R$: it never reaches the wall. The
certified mode is therefore an interior one, and the wall is not what holds it up. Beyond about $3R$
the computation ceases to mean anything --- at $4R$ it returns $\sn{6.7}{15}$ with the mode at
$0.04R$ --- because the degree-30 field is then evaluated far outside the interval on which it was
fitted; that is a property of the fit, not of the column, and it is why the sweep stops at $3R$.

\subsubsection{The chain}\label{sec:stageb-chain}

The proof is the following chain. Steps whose proofs are a line are given here; the five that are
not are stated with their certified values and proved in the supplementary document, as its items
S1--S5, each of which is self-contained and is named at the step that uses it. The computations are
described in Section~\ref{sec:stageb-arith} and, item by item with their falsification tests, in
Section S6 of the supplement.

\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{The operator, its self-adjointness, and its compact resolvent.} Let $\mathcal{H}$ and
$\mathcal{V}$ be the closures, in $L^2(Q)^3$ and in $H^1(Q)^3$ respectively, of all divergence-free
fields compactly supported in $D_{r_w}$ --- all azimuthal modes, not only $(m,k)$ --- and let
$s[u,v] := \int_Q \nabla u : \overline{\nabla v}$ on $\mathcal{V}$. Then $s$ is a densely defined,
symmetric, closed form on $\mathcal{H}$, so Kato's first representation theorem
\cite[Thm.\ VI-2.1]{K80} defines a unique
self-adjoint $S \ge 0$ with $D(S)\subset \mathcal{V}$ and $s[u,v] = \langle Su, v\rangle$. Freezing
$z$ and applying the two-dimensional Poincare inequality on $D_{r_w}$ gives
$S \ge (j_{0,1}/r_w)^2 > 0$; on the $(m,k)$ mode one has in addition
$\|\partial_z u\|^2 = k^2\|u\|^2$, and the two together give $\lambda/k^2 \ge 1 + (j_{0,1}/X)^2$, the
$1$ coming from the axial derivative and not from Poincare. Restriction to the
fundamental domain $D_{r_w}\times(0, 2\pi/k)$ is an isometry on $L^2$ and on $H^1$ onto a bounded
domain of $\mathbb{R}^3$ satisfying the cone condition, where Rellich-Kondrachov applies
\cite[Thm.\ 6.3]{AF03}; hence $\mathcal{V} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{H}$ is compact. Since $S^{-1}$
maps $\mathcal{H}$ boundedly into
$\mathcal{V}$ (from $s[u,u] = \langle f, u\rangle$ with $u = S^{-1}f$), it is compact as the composition of a
bounded and a compact map, so the spectrum of $S$ is a discrete set of eigenvalues of finite
multiplicity \cite[III-\S6.8, Thm.\ III-6.29]{K80} and, $S^{-1}$ being compact and self-adjoint,
$\mathcal{H}$ has an orthonormal eigenbasis with
$0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \cdots \to \infty$. Rotations about the axis
and axial translations act as unitaries preserving $\mathcal{V}$ and $s$, so they commute with $S$ and reduce it
\cite[III-\S5.6, V-\S3.9]{K80}; the part of $S$ in the reducing subspace $H_{m,k}$ is self-adjoint,
because $(S \pm i)^{-1}$ commutes with the corresponding projection and therefore maps $H_{m,k}$ onto
$D(S)\cap H_{m,k}$, and has compact resolvent; from here on $S$, $H$ and $\{\phi_j\}$ always mean
that part, that mode space and its eigenbasis. No identification of $D(S)$ with an $H^2$ space is
made, and none is used anywhere below; no boundary regularity theory enters.
\item \emph{$T$ is bounded, and $A$ is closed with compact resolvent.} Since $U_r \equiv 0$, advection
acts on the mode as multiplication by $ia(r)$ and $T = P_H(a + C)$ is bounded, with
$\|T\| \le \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_r \sigma_{\max}(T_{\mathrm{loc}}(r))$,
$T_{\mathrm{loc}} = a I + C_{\mathrm{loc}}$. Hence $A = -iS + T$ is a bounded perturbation of a normal
operator with compact resolvent: it is closed on $D(S)$, its spectrum is a discrete set of eigenvalues
of finite algebraic multiplicity, and for $|\operatorname{Re} z| > \|T\|$ the Neumann series gives
$(A-z)^{-1}$ compact. There is no continuous spectrum for $\nu > 0$.
\item \emph{Completeness and simplicity of the certified segment.} This is Lemma~S1 of the
supplement, proved there, whose part (ii) is Lemma A of Section~\ref{sec:stageb-axis} below and whose
determinant algebra is Lemma S1.1 of the supplement. Its statement:
under step 1, $\lambda > 1$ is an eigenvalue of $S$ on $H_{m,k}$ if and only if $\Delta(x) = 0$ with
$x = X\sqrt{\lambda - 1}$, where $\Delta$ is the $3\times 3$ wall determinant of the ansatz
$\phi = \alpha_+ J_{m+1}(\kappa r)e_+ + \alpha_- J_{m-1}(\kappa r)e_- + \alpha_z J_m(\kappa r)e_z
+ \lambda^{-1}c\,\nabla g$, $g = I_m(kr)e^{i(m\theta + kz)}$, $\kappa^2 = \lambda - k^2$, the
multiplicity being $\dim\ker A_3(x)$; every eigenfunction is of that form and is real-analytic on
$\overline{Q}$. The $H^2$ and $H^4$ memberships used in steps 11 and 12 are read off these formulas,
not obtained from a regularity theorem.
\item \emph{The certified Stokes spectrum.} The determinant $\Delta$ is expanded exactly and evaluated
in ball arithmetic \cite{J17}: $29278$ sign changes on $[2, 45993]$ from $\sn{2.3}{6}$ certified scan
points, each bracket bisected with certified signs, and the argument principle on
$(2, 45993)\times(-2,2)$ encloses the winding number as $29278 \pm \sn{1.6}{-22}$. The count equals
the number of brackets, so every zero in the rectangle is real and simple and none is missed;
separately $\Delta > 0$ on $(0,2]$. With step 3, the mode Stokes spectrum is complete and simple
through $\lambda/k^2 \ge \sn{6.97}{5}$, and in particular $\lambda_M \le 47997.288158$,
$\lambda_{M+1} \ge 48009.746020$, $\lambda_{N+1} \ge 208193.490748$ at $N = 16000$.
(\texttt{stokes\_rigorous\_L.py}; 371 s.)
\item \emph{The Galerkin matrix.} $T_{ij} = \langle T\phi_j, \phi_i\rangle$, $i,j \le M$, by
Gauss-Legendre quadrature with Arb nodes and weights \cite{JM18} and the analyticity remainder of
\cite[Thm.\ 19.3, Gauss case]{T13}, the Bessel factors bounded on the Bernstein ellipse and the polynomial field
enclosed by an exact rational Taylor shift to each panel centre followed by ball Horner. All 256 block
pairs: the Gram enclosure contains the identity on every pair (maximum deviation and radius
$\sn{2.5}{-15}$), normalizations have maximum relative radius $\sn{7.2}{-16}$, and the entry radii
run from $\sn{1.60}{-16}$ to $\sn{3.57}{-13}$ with mean $\sn{4.20}{-14}$. (\texttt{tmatrix\_block.py}; 7.4 core-hours.)
\item \emph{The approximate eigenpair.} $(\mu, w)$ is an eigenpair of the floating-point midpoint of
that matrix, with residual $\sn{3.91}{-13}$; $\mu$ and the components of $w$ are exact binary64 data
of the theorem, not approximations of anything, and $\|w\|^2$ differs from 1 by at most
$\sn{3}{-16}$, which is why the normalization is written $\langle u, w\rangle = \|w\|^2$. The independently certified Krawczyk
enclosure of the collocation pencil at $N = 100$, the resolution whose wall $r_{\max}\cos(\pi/4N)$
carries the same cosine factor as $r_w$, has centre $-17.525873540 + 25.425171865\,i$ and radius
$\sn{2.6}{-11}$ in these units, agreeing with $\mu$ to $\sn{5.0}{-9}$; by (G1) this is a cross-check,
not an input.
\item \emph{The bordered inverse on the block.} Let
$B_{11} := \begin{pmatrix} P(A - \mu)P & -w \\ \langle\cdot, w\rangle & 0\end{pmatrix}$ on
$\operatorname{range}P \times \mathbb{C}$. Then $\|B_{11}^{-1}\| \le \tilde K_h \le 1.2246711$. The
bound is a verified $\sigma_{\min}$: a floating Cholesky of the real $15\,366$-dimensional embedding
of $B_m^{H}B_m - tI$ succeeds, which by \cite[Thm.\ 10.3]{H02} and \cite{R06} certifies
$\lambda_{\min}(B_m^{H}B_m) \ge t = 0.666747054$ once the backward error and the product enclosure are
accounted for. Lemma S2.6 of the supplement then transports this over the whole interval family:
with $R$ the stored radius matrix of $B_{11}$, $\|R\|_2 \le \min(\|R\|_F, \sqrt{\|R\|_1\|R\|_\infty})
= \sn{4.932}{-10}$, bounded in the run by its outward-rounded accumulation $\sn{5.04}{-10}$, so that
by the perturbation form of Weyl's inequality \cite[Thm.\ 3.3.16(c)]{HJ91}
$\sigma_{\min} \ge \sqrt{t} - \sn{5.04}{-10} \ge 0.8165458059$ and
$\tilde K_h \le 1/0.8165458059 \le 1.2246711$. (\texttt{kh\_block.py}; 210 s, 3.1 GB.)
\item \emph{Block decomposition and the bound on $K$.} Write $\mathcal{B}$ for the bordered operator of
step 14 and $Q_\perp := I - P$. Since $P$ is a spectral projection of $S$, $PSQ_\perp = Q_\perp SP = 0$,
so $\mathcal{B}$ has the $2\times2$ block form with off-diagonal blocks $PTQ_\perp$ and $Q_\perp TP$
and corner $\mathcal{B}_{22} = Q_\perp(A - \mu)Q_\perp$. Two elementary bounds control the corner: the
normal part $D := Q_\perp(-iS - \mu)Q_\perp$ has $\|D^{-1}\| = 1/d_M$ with
$d_M = \bigl((\operatorname{Re}\mu)^2 + (\lambda_{M+1} + \operatorname{Im}\mu)^2\bigr)^{1/2}
\ge 48035.17$, and, since $a$ is real,
$\operatorname{Im}\langle \mathcal{B}_{22}u, u\rangle \le -c_\perp\|u\|^2$ with
$c_\perp := \lambda_{M+1} + \operatorname{Im}\mu - \|C\| \ge 47802.92$. The second bound gives more
than an estimate: $D^{-1}$ is compact on $\operatorname{range}Q_\perp$, being the norm limit of its
finite-rank truncations, so $I + D^{-1}Q_\perp T Q_\perp$ is Fredholm of index zero; the numerical-range
bound makes it injective, hence bijective, so
$\mathcal{B}_{22} = D(I + D^{-1}Q_\perp T Q_\perp)$ is boundedly invertible and
$\|\mathcal{B}_{22}^{-1}\| \le e := 1/c_\perp$. The Schur complement then gives, with
$t_{12} := \|PTQ_\perp\|$, $t_{21} := \|Q_\perp TP\|$, $Z := PTQ_\perp \mathcal{B}_{22}^{-1}Q_\perp TP$,
$\theta := \tilde K_h\|Z\|$ and $s := \tilde K_h/(1-\theta)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:stageb-K}
   \theta < 1 \ \Longrightarrow\ K \ \le\ \left\|
   \begin{pmatrix} s & s\,t_{12}e \\ e\,t_{21}s & e + e^2 t_{21}s\,t_{12}\end{pmatrix}\right\|_2 .
\end{equation}
(Proposition S2 of the supplement, with the lemmas and propositions S2.1--S2.5 that precede it and,
for the compactness of $D^{-1}$, Lemma S1.2.)
\item \emph{The pointwise constants.} By Lemma S5 of the supplement, with $F := aI + C^{*}$ written in
Cartesian components, $F$ is a
matrix field whose entries are polynomials in $(x,y)$ of degree at most 60 with coefficients in
$\mathbb{Q} + i\mathbb{Q}$, because $\Omega$ and $W$ are even polynomials in $r$ and hence
$\Omega'/r$, $W'/r$ are polynomials in $x^2+y^2$; in particular $\partial_z F = 0$, every
$\partial^\alpha F$ is such a polynomial matrix, and the Leibniz expansions of steps 11--12 are
legitimate. The jet $\Theta_n := \max_{|\alpha| = n}\sup_{\overline{Q}}\|\partial^\alpha F\|_{op}$ is
computed by rotational covariance (which collapses the two-dimensional supremum to a one-dimensional
adaptive bisection with an enclosed angular table), an exact integer Taylor shift of the field to each
panel centre, and the exact largest eigenvalue of the $3\times3$ Hermitian $A^{H}A$:
\[
   \Theta_0 = \|T\| \le 506.548892, \quad \Theta_1 \le 2482.955855, \quad
   \Theta_2 \le 21447.36325, \quad \Theta_4 \le 906972.8975 ,
\]
together with $\gamma := 2(1+m^2/X^2)/(X\varrho) \le 0.0366439622$ with
$\varrho = I_m'(X)/I_m(X)$, $\mu_w = 0.1905558538$, $\mu_2 = 1.408070809$,
$\alpha = \pi/(3X) \ge 0.0190087462$, $\|h\|/\|\nabla g\| \le 44.4999489$ and
$\|h^{*}\|/\|\nabla g\| \le 31.2324161$ with $h := F^{*}\nabla g$, $h^{*} := F\nabla g$. A free
correctness test of the quadrature is that its own value of $\|\nabla g\|^2$ encloses the closed form
$X\varrho$, which it does to 27 digits. ($\Theta_3$ does not appear: see step 11.)
(\texttt{stageb\_consts.py}; 1.5 s.) The constant $\|C\| \le 232.2489$ used in step 8 comes from a
separate subdivision in interval arithmetic (\texttt{tnorm\_rigorous.py}), taken over the slightly
larger disc $r \le r_{\max}\cos(\pi/400)$, which contains $\overline{Q}$; a supremum over a superset
is an upper bound on the supremum over $\overline{Q}$, so the constant is valid and conservative.
\item \emph{The computed coupling.} With $N = 16000$, the two $M\times(N-M)$ strips
$PT(P_N - P)$ and $(P_N - P)TP$ are computed in ball arithmetic by the same quadrature machinery as
step 5, in 17 column blocks, $\sn{1.3}{8}$ entries, the Gram enclosure containing zero on all 272
block pairs. Their operator norms are then certified by
$\|A\|_2 \le \|A_{\mathrm{mid}}\|_2 + \|A_{\mathrm{rad}}\|_2$ (Lemma S2.6 of the supplement), with
$\lambda_{\max}(A_{\mathrm{mid}}^{T}A_{\mathrm{mid}}) \le c$ established by a floating Cholesky of
$cI - A_{\mathrm{mid}}^{T}A_{\mathrm{mid}}$ under \cite[Thm.\ 10.3]{H02}, and the radius matrices
bounded by $\|A_{\mathrm{rad}}\|_2 \le \sn{8.6381}{-10}$ and $\sn{8.6243}{-10}$ respectively
(Frobenius $\sn{9.814}{-10}$, $\sn{9.812}{-10}$):
\[
   \|PT(P_N-P)\| \le 140.320484, \qquad \|(P_N-P)TP\| \le 140.228256 ,
\]
valid for every matrix of the stored ball family. (\texttt{tmatrix\_rect.py}, 24 core-hours;
\texttt{ropnorm.py}, 389 s.)
\item \emph{The coupling tail (Proposition T2).} The remaining coupling is
$\tau_N := \|(I - P_N)T^{*}P\|_{HS}$ and $\tau'_N := \|(I-P_N)TP\|_{HS}$, which bound
$t_{12} \le \|PT(P_N-P)\| + \tau_N$ and $t_{21} \le \|(P_N-P)TP\| + \tau'_N$ and the tail of $Z$. They
are estimated by a two-level identity: for $v \in H^2(Q)^3$ and any index $j$,
\[
   (\lambda_j - \lambda_i)\langle v, \phi_j\rangle
   = \langle -(\Delta + \lambda_i)v, \phi_j\rangle
     - X\, v(X)\cdot\overline{\partial_n\phi_j(X)}
     + \overline{c_j}\,\langle v, \nabla g\rangle ,
\]
$q_j = c_j g$ being the pressure of $\phi_j$; applied twice, once to $f_i := F\phi_i$ and once to
$(\Delta + \lambda_i)f_i$, with one integration by parts that cancels the Hessian of $\phi_i$ against
the third-derivative terms of $F$ exactly. The inputs are the jet of step 9, a Rellich identity
bounding the wall shear, a wall identity bounding the pressure amplitudes by
$|c_j|\,\|\nabla g\| \le \sqrt{\gamma(\lambda_j-1)} + \gamma$ for \emph{all} $j$, and a Weyl-type
lower bound $\lambda_j \ge 1 + \alpha^2(j-5)^2$. No Hessian estimate, no third-derivative constant and
no elliptic regularity on $Q$ enter. Evaluated in ball arithmetic at $N = 16000$ with the certified
eigenvalues of step 4,
\[
   \tau_{16000} \le 84.882443, \qquad \tau'_{16000} \le 83.185699 .
\]
(Proposition S3 of the supplement, with Lemmas S3.1--S3.5; evaluation in
\texttt{stageb\_scalars\_iv.py}.)
\item \emph{The defect (Proposition T3).} Since $w \in \operatorname{range}P$ and $P$ is a spectral
projection of $S$, $\delta^2 = \|(A - \mu)w\|^2 = \|(PAP - \mu)w\|^2 + \|(I-P)Tw\|^2$ exactly. The
first term is certified from the stored interval matrix at $\le \sn{9.124907}{-11}$; it is eight
orders below the second, and the Pythagorean sum is carried out below rather than dropped. The second is a
single-vector version of the identity of step 11 applied at shift zero to $v := F^{*}w$, which
vanishes at the wall; at shift zero the denominator is $\lambda_j$ rather than
$\lambda_j - \lambda_i$, so $N = M$ is admissible and the bound needs no rectangle. It reduces to four
scalar families built from $w$ and the certified per-mode data --- the moments
$m_p = (\sum_i \lambda_i^p|w_i|^2)^{1/2}$, the pressure moments
$\gamma_p = |\sum_i \lambda_i^p w_i c_i|\,\|\nabla g\|$, the wall shear
$d_w = |\sum_i w_i\,\partial_n\phi_i(X)|$ and $\pi_0 = \langle w, h^{*}\rangle$ --- all evaluated as
signed Arb enclosures, the signs being licensed by an orientation certificate that matches the mode
field of every one of the 7682 modes, at three quadrature nodes and in all three components, against
the exactly serialized field that built the matrix of step 5 (69138 ball tests, all overlapping, worst
separation $\sn{4.1}{17}$ combined radii). The result is
\[
   \text{part two} \le \sn{8.017047}{-3}, \qquad\text{hence}\qquad
   \delta = \sqrt{(\sn{9.124907}{-11})^2 + (\text{part two})^2} \le \sn{8.017048}{-3} .
\]
A cancellation-free variant, in which three of the four families are replaced by sums of absolute
values, gives $\delta \le \sn{1.095725}{-2}$ and still closes the acceptance below.
(Proposition S4 of the supplement, with Lemma S4.1; \texttt{rdefect.py}, \texttt{t3\_balls.py};
350 s.)
\item \emph{The assembly.} With $d_N \ge 208218.91$ the Schur term splits as
$Z = Z_0^{(N)} + R_N + (Z - Z_0)$, the computed band, the tail beyond $N$, and the resolvent
correction, bounded respectively by
$\|PT(P_N-P)\|\,\|(P_N-P)TP\|/d_M$, $\tau_N\tau'_N/d_N$ and
$t_{12}t_{21}\|T\|/(c_\perp d_M)$. In interval arithmetic:
\begin{center}
\begin{tabular}{lll}
$\|Z_0^{(N)}\|$ & $\le 0.4096352$ & computed band, $M < j \le N$\\
$\|R_N\|$ & $\le 0.0339115$ & tail, $j > N$, from step 11\\
$\|Z - Z_0\|$ & $\le 0.0110993$ & with $t_{12} \le 225.2030$, $t_{21} \le 223.4140$\\[2pt]
$\|Z\|$ & $\le 0.4546459$ & \\
$\theta = \tilde K_h\|Z\|$ & $\le 0.5567917$ & $< 1$\\
$K$ & $\le 2.7632556$ & by \eqref{eq:stageb-K}\\
$\beta = 4K^2\delta$ & $\le 0.2448593$ & $< 1$\\
$\rho$ & $\le \sn{2.370604}{-2}$ & $= 47.42\ \mathrm{s}^{-1}$
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
Each line of the table is independently outward-rounded from the unrounded interval chain, so the
table is not to be re-composed: recomputing $K$ from the printed $\theta$, $t_{12}$, $t_{21}$ and
$\tilde K_h$ returns $2.7632562$, above the printed $2.7632556$, which is nonetheless a valid bound
on the true $K = 2.76325554$.
The tail is the only term entitled to the weight $1/d_N$ rather than $1/d_M$, and it is entitled to it
because $D^{-1}$ restricted to $\operatorname{range}(I - P_N)$ has norm $1/d_N$. Nothing turns on that
gain: with the pessimistic weight $1/d_M$ throughout, the acceptance still admits any tail up to
$101.6$, against the certified $84.88$.
The criterion is insensitive to most of these inputs and tight in three. Holding the others at their
certified values, $\beta = 1$ is reached when the two strip bounds rise by 20 percent, when
$\tilde K_h$ rises by 29 percent, or when $\lambda_{M+1}$ falls by 29 percent; whereas the tail may
rise by 144 percent, $\delta$ may be 4.1 times larger and $\|T\|$ may be wrong by a factor 17.
Degrading every input simultaneously in its unfavourable direction, the criterion closes up to a
common relative degradation of 7.6 percent (all nine inputs, $\lambda_{N+1}$ included); that, rather
than the factor 4.1 in $\beta$, is the honest
robustness figure, because $\theta$ sits at $0.56$ and $K$ carries the factor $(1-\theta)^{-1}$, which
amplifies every input error.
(\texttt{accept\_iv.py}, \texttt{stageb\_scalars\_iv.py}.)
\item \emph{The fixed point.} Let $\mathcal{B}: D(S)\times\mathbb{C} \to H\times\mathbb{C}$,
$\mathcal{B}(v,\eta) := ((A - \mu)v - \eta w,\ \langle v, w\rangle)$, and let $K$ be as in
\eqref{eq:stageb-K}, so that $\|(v,\eta)\| \le K\|\mathcal{B}(v,\eta)\|$ in the Euclidean norms
$\|(v,\eta)\|^2 = \|v\|^2 + |\eta|^2$. Put $d := (A - \mu)w$, $\delta = \|d\|$, and seek
$\omega = \mu + \eta$, $u = w + v$ with $\langle v, w\rangle = 0$. Then $(A-\omega)u = 0$ is
equivalent to $\mathcal{B}(v,\eta) = (-d + \eta v,\ 0)$, i.e.\ to the fixed-point equation
$(v,\eta) = \mathcal{T}(v,\eta) := \mathcal{B}^{-1}(-d + \eta v,\ 0)$, whose solutions automatically
satisfy $\langle v, w\rangle = 0$. On the closed ball of radius $\rho$,
$\|\mathcal{T}(v,\eta)\| \le K(\delta + |\eta|\|v\|) \le K(\delta + \rho^2)$ and
\[
   \|\mathcal{T}(v,\eta) - \mathcal{T}(v',\eta')\|
   \le K\bigl(|\eta|\,\|v - v'\| + |\eta - \eta'|\,\|v'\|\bigr)
   \le \sqrt{2}\,K\rho\,\|(v,\eta) - (v',\eta')\| .
\]
With $\rho = 2K\delta/(1 + \sqrt{1-\beta})$ and $\beta = 4K^2\delta < 1$ one has
$K\rho^2 - \rho + K\delta = 0$, so $\mathcal{T}$ maps the ball into itself, and
$2K\rho = 1 - \sqrt{1-\beta} < 1$, so $\mathcal{T}$ is a contraction there. Banach's theorem gives a
unique fixed point in the ball, and hence a unique pair $(\omega, u)$ with
$|\omega - \mu|^2 + \|u - w\|^2 \le \rho^2$ and $\langle u - w, w\rangle = 0$; $u = w + v \ne 0$
because $\|u - w\| \le \rho < \|w\|$, and $\langle u, w\rangle = \|w\|^2$. This proves Theorem 2,
modulo Lemma S1 and Propositions S2, S3 and S4 of the supplement, which are proved there, and
Lemma S5, which licenses the Leibniz expansions of steps 11 and 12. $\square$
\end{enumerate}

\subsubsection{The axis condition at the first azimuthal mode}\label{sec:stageb-axis}

Step 3 asserts that every eigenfunction of $S$ on $H_{m,k}$ lies in the three-dimensional span of the
regular Bessel solutions and $\nabla g$, and in particular that its pressure carries no singular
modified-Bessel part. For $|m| \ge 2$ that exclusion follows from square-integrability alone, since the
singular pressure then contributes a term of order $r^{-(m-1)}$ to a component that must lie in
$L^2(r\,dr)$. At $m = 1$, the case used here, it does not: the singular terms can be cancelled between
the two Bessel families and what remains is square-integrable. The following lemma repairs the step,
using only $D(S) \subset V \subset H^1(Q)^3$, which step 1 supplies.

\medskip\noindent \textbf{Lemma A (axis exclusion at $m = 1$).}\label{lem:K}
\emph{Let $m = 1$, $k \ne 0$, $\lambda \ne 0$. Let $\phi \in H^1(Q)^3$ be of mode type $(m,k)$ with
$\operatorname{div}\phi = 0$, and suppose $(\Delta + \lambda)\phi = \nabla q$ in
$\mathcal{D}'(Q)$ for some distribution $q$. Then $q = c\,I_m(kr)e^{i(m\theta + kz)}$ for some
$c \in \mathbb{C}$, with no $K_m$ part, and $\phi$ lies in the span of the two regular Bessel solutions
and $\nabla q$.}

\medskip\noindent \emph{Proof.} (i) Taking the divergence, $\Delta q = 0$ in $\mathcal{D}'(Q)$, so $q$
is harmonic, hence smooth inside $Q$ by Weyl's lemma, and equivariant under the two commuting groups
up to an additive constant, which vanishes because $(m,k) \ne (0,0)$. Thus
$q = Q(r)e^{i(m\theta + kz)}$ with $(rQ')' = (m^2/r + k^2 r)Q$, i.e.\
$Q = a\,I_m(kr) + b\,K_m(kr)$.

(ii) Set $w := \phi - \lambda^{-1}\nabla q$. Since $\Delta\nabla q = \nabla\Delta q = 0$, $w$ solves
$(\Delta + \lambda)w = 0$, so by interior regularity and the mode structure its components
$w_+ := w_r + iw_\theta$, $w_- := w_r - iw_\theta$, $w_z$ solve Bessel equations of orders $m+1 = 2$,
$m-1 = 0$ and $m = 1$ in the argument $\kappa r$, $\kappa^2 = \lambda - k^2$:
$w_+ = \alpha_+ J_2(\kappa r) + \beta_+ Y_2(\kappa r)$ and similarly in the other two slots.

(iii) The Cartesian components of the mode carry azimuthal indices $m+1 = 2$ for $w_+$, $m-1 = 0$ for
$w_-$ and $m = 1$ for $w_z$, and for a Cartesian component $F(r)e^{in\theta}e^{ikz}$ one has
$|\nabla(\cdot)|^2 = |F'|^2 + n^2|F|^2/r^2 + k^2|F|^2$. Membership in $H^1(Q)$ therefore forces
$\int_0 |F|^2\,dr/r < \infty$ whenever $n \ne 0$, and $\int_0 |F'|^2 r\,dr < \infty$ always.

(iv) The ``$+$'' slot alone forces $b = 0$. With
$(\nabla q)_+ = Q' - (m/r)Q = k\,(a I_{m+1}(kr) - b K_{m+1}(kr))$,
\[
   \phi_+ = \lambda^{-1}k\bigl[a I_2(kr) - b K_2(kr)\bigr]
            + \alpha_+ J_2(\kappa r) + \beta_+ Y_2(\kappa r).
\]
By \cite[(10.31.1)]{DLMF}, $K_2(z) = 2/z^2 - 1/2 + O(z^2\log z)$, and by \cite[(10.8.1)]{DLMF},
$Y_2(z) = -4/(\pi z^2) - 1/\pi + O(z^2\log z)$, while $I_2$ and $J_2$ are $O(r^2)$. In both expansions
the logarithm first enters at order $z^2\log z$, so the only obstructions in this slot are the
$r^{-2}$ and $r^0$ coefficients. Since $n = 2$ here, step (iii) requires
$\int_0 |\phi_+|^2 dr/r < \infty$, which annihilates both:
\[
   r^{-2}:\quad -\frac{2b}{\lambda k} - \frac{4\beta_+}{\pi\kappa^2} = 0, \qquad
   r^{0}:\quad \frac{kb}{2\lambda} - \frac{\beta_+}{\pi} = 0 ,
\]
that is, $\beta_+ = -\pi\kappa^2 b/(2\lambda k)$ and $\beta_+ = \pi k b/(2\lambda)$. Equating,
$-\kappa^2 b/k = kb$, i.e.\ $b(\kappa^2 + k^2) = b\lambda = 0$, so $b = 0$ and $\beta_+ = 0$.
Equivalently, the $2\times2$ system for $(b, \beta_+)$ has determinant
$(2/(\lambda\pi))(\kappa^2 + k^2)/\kappa^2 = 2/(\pi\kappa^2) \ne 0$. (For
$\kappa^2 < 0$ the same two conditions, with $(J,Y)$ replaced by $(I,K)$, give
$b(|\kappa|^2 - k^2) = -b\lambda = 0$; for $\kappa = 0$ the $r^0$ term is uncancelled and $b = 0$
directly.)

(v) With $b = 0$ the pressure gradient is regular, and the remaining singular coefficients die slot by
slot: in the $z$ slot $Y_1(\kappa r) \sim -2/(\pi\kappa r)$ violates the condition of step (iii) at
$n = 1$, so $\beta_z = 0$; in the ``$-$'' slot $Y_0(\kappa r) \sim (2/\pi)\log r$ has derivative of
order $1/r$, and $\int_0 r^{-2}\,r\,dr = \infty$, so $\beta_- = 0$. What remains is
$\phi \in \operatorname{span}\{$toroidal, poloidal, $\nabla g\}$, and the divergence-free condition
reduces to the single linear relation of step 3. $\square$

\medskip\noindent The mechanism is that $K_2(kr)$ and $Y_2(\kappa r)$ carry different arguments, so
their two singular coefficients cannot be matched simultaneously; the obstruction is exactly
$\kappa^2 + k^2 = \lambda \ne 0$, which the positivity of $S$ from step 1 supplies. Lemma A is used
only in step 3, and only at $m = 1$; at $|m| \ge 2$ square-integrability suffices, and $m = 0$, which
this certificate does not use, genuinely differs, the singular orders in the two transverse slots
coinciding there.

\subsubsection{Arithmetic assumptions, and reproduction}\label{sec:stageb-arith}

The computations are of three kinds: ball (midpoint-radius) arithmetic in Arb through python-flint
\cite{J17}, with rigorous Gauss-Legendre nodes \cite{JM18}; interval arithmetic in mpmath; and
double-precision linear algebra whose rounding errors are accounted a posteriori by the classical
$\gamma_n$ inequalities \cite{H02,R10}. The assumptions are:

\begin{itemize}
\item[(A1)] IEEE-754 binary64 arithmetic, with overflow detected rather than prevented and underflow
floored at values checked by inspection.
\item[(A2)] The classical inner-product model for real BLAS: each entry of a real binary64 matrix
product is one inner product evaluated in some order, with or without a fused multiply-add. No
Strassen-type algorithm. This is the assumption INTLAB makes, and it is what licenses the
$|fl(PQ) - PQ| \le \gamma_n |P||Q|$ bounds used for every product enclosure and for the Cholesky
backward error \cite[Thm.\ 10.3]{H02}.
\item[(A3)] Correctness of the interval libraries: Arb/python-flint, mpmath's interval arithmetic, and
the project's own midpoint-radius matrix module, whose rounding bounds are checked against exact
rational arithmetic in its test suite.
\end{itemize}

The two Cholesky-based steps (7 and 10) are order-independent in the sense of
\cite[Lemma 8.4 and Thm.\ 10.3]{H02},
so neither the blocked LAPACK factorization nor a self-contained row factorization is load-bearing;
both were run and agree.

Reproduction. The scripts, logs and certified data files accompany the paper as supplementary
material, together with the supplement, whose Section S6 describes each computation, its falsification
tests and its hash. The two large intermediate
objects are not distributed: the $M\times M$ Galerkin matrix and the $M\times(N-M)$ rectangle occupy
5.9 and 5.8 GiB, and are rebuilt from the scripts in 7.4 and 24 core-hours respectively on one core,
with peak resident memory 1.8 and 1.7 GB. Everything downstream of them is minutes: the certified
Stokes spectrum 371 s, the bordered inverse 210 s, the strip norms 389 s, the defect 350 s, the
pointwise constants 1.5 s, the tail and the assembly under a second, and a single driver
(\texttt{stageb\_verify\_all.py}) runs all of it and prints the constants of the table above in the
order the assembly uses them. The SHA-256 of every certified input, log and script, and a directory
digest for each of the two stores, are listed in \texttt{SUPPLEMENT\_MANIFEST.txt}
(982 files, 11.7 GiB), which \texttt{stageb\_manifest.py} regenerates.

\subsubsection{Corrections}\label{sec:stageb-corrections}

Three bounds that were adequate at 200 basis functions were inadequate at 7682, and we record them
because the discipline they impose --- recompute every constant by a second, independent route at the
size actually used --- is what the rest of this subsection rests on.

First, an early bound on $\|T\|$ read the largest singular value off $T_{\mathrm{loc}}^{H}T_{\mathrm{loc}}$
assumed block diagonal. It is not: the entry $(1,3)$ equals $i a d$ with $d = W'$, so the closed form
underestimates $\sigma_{\max}$ by between 0.02 and 0.3 percent on the matrices that occur here, and a
bound taking a minimum over it could in principle fall below the true supremum. The figure is
withdrawn and replaced by $\Theta_0 \le 506.548892$ of step 9, computed by an independent route. The
same script's bound on $\|C\|$ survives, and is used in step 8: for $C_{\mathrm{loc}}$ the matrix
$C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{H}C_{\mathrm{loc}} = \operatorname{diag}(c^2 + d^2,\ 4\Omega^2,\ 0)$ with
$c = 2\Omega + r\Omega'$ is genuinely diagonal, the offending entry being proportional to $a$, which
is removed in $C$.

Second, the a-posteriori rounding-correction routine carries a guard limiting it to the number of
roundings its own proof covers, $\sn{4}{7}$; the Frobenius accumulation over a $7683\times7683$ matrix
counts $\sn{5.9}{7}$ and the first bordered inverse aborted. The guard was correct and the fix is by
composition rather than by weakening: applying the correction in chunks multiplies the inflation
factors, and the regression reproduces the $M = 200$ value bit-identically.

Third, the strip couplings were first bounded by their Hilbert-Schmidt norms, $229.74$ and $229.55$
against the operator norms $140.32$ and $140.23$ of step 10. That is the $\sqrt{\mathrm{rank}}$ cost of
bounding an operator norm by a Hilbert-Schmidt norm; harmless at $M = 200$, it is fatal at $M = 7682$,
where it makes $\theta > 1$ and the criterion vacuous. It was found by comparing the bound against the
floating-point operator norm of its own midpoints, and repaired post hoc by the certified
$\lambda_{\max}$ route of step 10, with no quadrature repeated. That route carries a deliberate
falsification test --- set the Cholesky shift a tenth of a percent below the floating-point
$\lambda_{\max}$ and require breakdown, which occurs --- and it is exactly the test the first bound
would have failed.

\section{Nonlinear fate}
\label{sec:nl}

The $m = 1$ mode was seeded at 20 and 50 percent of the local swirl velocity on the Euler x28 state, at 20 percent on the viscous x144 state, and at 20 percent on the Euler x200 state, with $m = 0, 1, 2$ (and 3) carried and the Reynolds-stress feedback on the base.

\emph{On the Euler states the mode depletes the collapse.} Against the unperturbed collapse at matched times the axisymmetric amplitude lags: on Euler x28 by 0.8, 1.3, 2.1, 3.6 percent at 10, 13, 16, 21 percent of the remaining time with the 20 percent seed, and by 5 percent at 11 percent with the 50 percent seed, at which the axisymmetric swirl maximum stalls, at 1.062 times its value at the seeding time, while the three-dimensional swirl maximum stays flat at 1.9 times the axisymmetric one, the mode's own growth drops below its linear rate (0.266 against 0.35 on the co-evolving base at that time), and the $m = 2$ harmonic sits on the $\epsilon^2$ curve at $\sn{8}{-3}$ of the $m = 1$ energy without migrating. The x28 continuation reached 49 percent of the remaining time with a 22 percent lag and the three-dimensional swirl ratio flat at 1.37.

\emph{On the viscous state it does not, within the range we resolve.} At every output time the two runs share, the seeded run's axisymmetric amplitude agrees with the unperturbed collapse to better than 0.02 percent out to 23.9 percent of the remaining time, and to within 0.15 percent -- the reference's time-printing resolution, which is what limits the comparison there -- out to 34.6 percent. The same run, carried to 23.9 percent of the remaining time with three azimuthal modes, also tests whether the growth rolls up into an intensifying substructure. (We intended a second run from a random seed here. It was not performed: the nonlinear solver does not read the variable that was meant to select the seed, and the two logs are byte-identical. What follows is the localized-seed run, and the paper makes no claim about a random seed on the viscous base.) The three-dimensional vorticity peak rose from 1.04 to 1.71 times the axisymmetric peak while the axisymmetric amplitude ran 9 percent above the Type I line and the second harmonic stayed at two percent of the first. The end-state fields show the mode's energy density peaking on the ring (radius 0.98 of the swirl maximum's, height 0.91 of its) with half-widths of 0.7 to 0.8 collapse lengths, about thirty times the Burgers thickness $\sqrt{\nu (T - t)}$, and the swirl at that point exceeding its azimuthal mean by a factor 1.38. There is no compact off-axis maximum at the viscous scale, no Burgers-locked core and no climbing harmonics: the rising vorticity ratio is the linear family growing on a base whose amplitude it has not measurably touched. So on the viscous state the runs end with a symmetry-broken state that is still collapsing on the axisymmetric law, and neither a continued nor an arrested symmetry-broken collapse was reached before the computation ran out of resolution.

\emph{When the mode arrives.} A perturbation of relative size $\epsilon$ reaches order one after the base amplifies by $\epsilon^{-1/\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}}$, with $\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}} = \sigma\,(T-t) - 1/2$ the margin over the conservative threshold of Section~\ref{sec:thresh} and the estimate that of a supercritical mode saturating on its own Reynolds stress (Stuart-Watson \cite{SW60}; depletion of this general kind was found in Hou and Li's computation of Kerr's antiparallel tubes \cite{HL06,HL08}, by a mechanism of their own, geometric depletion of vortex stretching, which is not the one here). On the last measured points -- which for the co-evolving families are inside the unconverged window of Section~\ref{sec:res}, so the amplifications below are order-of-magnitude -- $\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$ is 0.34 for the long-wave $m = 1$ direction of the Euler x28 state, 0.68 for the long-wave direction of the viscous x144 state and 1.65 for its short-wave $m = 1$ family, so a one percent seed reaches order one after an amplification of about $\sn{8}{5}$, $\sn{9}{2}$ and 16 respectively. Because the threshold is conservative (Remark 1), these are upper bounds on the amplification required. On the viscous base that is well inside the range a computation resolves, and it is what the runs show: the mode reaches order one relative to the base swirl while the collapse continues.

\emph{The second harmonic is slaved, and the null that says so.} Only $m = 1$ is seeded, so $m = 2$ is born as its harmonic, and a test of whether a second instability has taken over must be read against the growth a mere harmonic would show. That growth obeys a one-line law.

\medskip\noindent\textbf{Lemma H (the harmonic-exponent law).} \emph{Let $a_2' = \lambda_2 a_2 + c\, a_1^2$ with $a_1 = a_1(0) e^{\lambda_1 t}$, $c \neq 0$, $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_1 = \sigma_1 > 0$ and $2\lambda_1 \neq \lambda_2$. Then}
\[
\kappa = \frac{d \log |a_2|^2}{d \log |a_1|^2} \longrightarrow \max\!\left(2, \frac{\sigma_2}{\sigma_1}\right), \qquad \sigma_2 = \operatorname{Re}\lambda_2 .
\]
\emph{In particular $\kappa$ settles above $2$ only if the second mode's own growth rate exceeds twice the first's.}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Proof.} The solution is $a_2 = c\,a_1(0)^2 e^{2\lambda_1 t}/(2\lambda_1 - \lambda_2) + K e^{\lambda_2 t}$. The faster exponential dominates $|a_2|^2$, whose exponent is therefore $\max(4\sigma_1, 2\sigma_2)$, while $\log|a_1|^2$ grows at $2\sigma_1$. \hfill$\square$

\medskip\noindent The forced part is the slaved harmonic and the homogeneous part is the second mode growing at its own rate; if $a_2(0) = 0$ the ratio approaches $2$ from above when $\sigma_2 < 2\sigma_1$. On the columnar rates of Section~\ref{sec:columnar}, $\sigma_2 / \sigma_1 = 0.98$, so the law predicts $\kappa \to 2$: a harmonic, not an independent rung. The runs are consistent with that and nothing stronger. The harmonic stays at $\sn{8}{-3}$ of the $m = 1$ energy on the Euler state and at two percent of the first mode on the viscous one, without migrating in wavenumber; we do not have a measurement of $\kappa$ with the error bars that would distinguish $2$ from $\sigma_2/\sigma_1$. The reason for stating the lemma is negative and methodological: a harmonic climbing from near zero towards the level its parent sustains shows a rising energy ratio and a fast transient growth, which is what a naive test of independence reads as independence. We ran such a test on the eight independent seeded runs, on criteria fixed in writing beforehand, and most runs passed it; two of the three criteria have no power against the null of Lemma H, and the verdict was withdrawn before it was reported. A test of a handoff between successive instability stages needs $\kappa$ measured against $\max(2, \sigma_2/\sigma_1)$ with the rates measured on the same states, and we do not report one here.

\section{The first-stage viscous continuation}
\label{sec:cont}

Hou computes his Navier-Stokes scenario in two stages: viscosity $\nu = \sn{5}{-4}$ from $t = 0$ to $t_0 = 0.00227375$, and $\nu = \sn{5}{-3}$ thereafter, the increase being made because $\sn{5}{-4}$ `is not strong enough to stabilize the shearing instability generated by the 3D Euler equations' \cite[Sec. 3]{H23b}. What we continue, and what every measurement in this section and in Section~\ref{sec:theorems} is made on, is his \emph{first-stage} solution, carried at $\nu = \sn{5}{-4}$ past $t_0$ without the increase. It is a different flow from his two-stage one after $t_0$, and we make no measurement on the second stage. The instability that made him raise the viscosity is the object of Sections~\ref{sec:euler}-\ref{sec:columnar}.

\subsection{The singular time and the amplitude exponent}
\label{sec:fit}

Hou's own caveat \cite[Sec. 3.4]{H23b} is that the Type I rate inequalities `would be almost impossible to verify numerically since it requires the exact value of $T$'. We fit $T$ by the log-derivative method: for $A \sim C (T - t)^{-p}$ the ratio $A / A'$ equals $(T - t) / p$, linear in $t$ with slope $-1/p$ and zero at $T$, so sliding-window fits give $p$ and $T$ together with nothing assumed, and Luo and Hou's criterion \cite{LH14a,LH14b} is that both stop moving as the window slides toward $T$. On the resolved snapshots of the continuation (Section~\ref{sec:map}) four-point windows ending at 0.002281, 0.002282, 0.002283, 0.002284 and 0.0022845 give $p = 1.49$, 1.37, 1.19, 1.04, 1.05 with $T = 0.0022888$, 0.0022881, 0.0022872, 0.0022865, 0.0022866, and five-point windows ending at 0.0022845, 0.002285 and 0.0022853 give $p = 1.04$, 1.00, 1.06 with $T = 0.0022865$, 0.0022864, 0.0022866: both have stopped moving over the last three windows. We quote
\[
p = 1.03 \pm 0.03, \qquad T = 0.0022865 \pm \sn{1}{-7},
\]
and use this $T$ for every collapse-unit quantity in the paper.

The pair is strongly correlated, and the correlation is larger than the trend it is fitted to. Recomputing the constants of Section~\ref{sec:consts} directly from the archived snapshots gives $A\,(T-t)$ at the fitted $T$ that rises to a plateau near 3.85 by x72 and then falls by 2 percent to x329; since $A(T-t) \propto A^{1-1/p}$, that fall implies $p = 0.98$ over the late range, while moving $T$ by $+\sn{1}{-7}$, one part in $10^4$ and within the fit's own uncertainty, turns the same 2 percent fall into a 4 percent rise and $p$ into 1.05. The exponent that the data support is therefore $p = 1.0 \pm 0.05$ jointly with $T = 0.0022865 \pm \sn{1}{-7}$, and no statement in this paper rests on the second decimal of either. We keep the log-derivative value as the quoted fit because it uses the amplitude history rather than two endpoints, and we flag that a reader who prefers the endpoint estimate gets 0.98 at the same $T$.

The exponent is not constant along the way, and measuring it locally resolves what would otherwise look like a disagreement with Section~\ref{sec:ns4}. Centred differences of $\log A$ against $\log(1/(T-t))$ on the fourteen recorded states from x3 to x92 give a local exponent that rises from 1.07 at x3 to a maximum of 1.33 near x25, which is why the base of the runs of Section~\ref{sec:ns4}, which advances from x9 through x25 while they proceed, carries an effective exponent of 1.2 to 1.4, and then falls monotonically through 1.12, 1.03 and 0.99 to 0.98 by x92. A fit over all fourteen returns 1.20 and a fit over the last six returns 1.007; the quoted $p = 1.03$ is the value settled on over the later, resolved range x131 to x331, which is a different and later set of states. So the amplitude approaches the Type I exponent from above, with a transient overshoot of about a third in the middle of the range. The earlier apparent $p \sim 1.8$ of a fixed-$T$ fit was the concave $A/A'$ of subleading corrections in the early windows, and a first reading of `falling Type I constants' from a $1/A$ fit with a drifting $T$ was retracted on this basis.

\subsection{The continuation and the front-following map}
\label{sec:map}

The first-stage solution was continued at $\nu = \sn{5}{-4}$ on a $513 \times 1024$ grid with a moving radial map and an axial map concentrated at the symmetry plane, from x25 to x217, with a twin at a different axial map and Courant number agreeing to 0.5 percent in amplitude through x217; past x217 the front's width fell to two cells and the twins diverged by 27 percent, and the run was stopped. A 2048-point restart from x131 with a three-times finer axial map read the front at three cells at x268, still grid-limited. The solver was then given a front-following axial map: a Gaussian point density centred on the vorticity maximum with a fifth of the points within three front widths, re-fitted with the radial rezone every hundred steps, the fields moved by exact sine-series evaluation; a map contrast above about 500 breaks the mapped Poisson solve, so the window is kept at three front widths (contrast about 140, symmetrization error $\sn{2}{-5}$), at which the restart reproduces the state to a percent.

On that map the same x222 state has a front $\sn{4.8}{-5}$ wide over ten cells where the coarse map had read $\sn{7.7}{-5}$ over three, and after one interval (x268) the front is $\sn{3.3}{-5}$ wide over nine cells. Re-evaluating the x268 state on a second map gives the error bars: front thickness $\pm 15$ percent, vorticity plateau $\pm 5$ percent, swirl constant $\pm 2$ percent from the grid, meridional constant $\pm 20$ percent, amplitude and its constants 0.5 percent.

With the window floor set at $\sn{1.5}{-4}$ (contrast 140 to 170) the continuation was carried on two grids (1536 and 2048 axial points) from x131 to x395, agreeing to 0.5 percent. The measurements of Sections~\ref{sec:consts}-\ref{sec:theorems} are made on the snapshots of that range, extended backwards to 9 times where the earlier grids supply resolved states; Table~\ref{tab:states} gives the range used for each quantity.

At about x400 ($T - t$ about $\sn{8}{-7}$, $\log(1/(T-t)) = 14.0$) the one-scale collapse ends: the primary front stalls (x395 to x382 over one output interval, $A(T-t)$ falling from 4.3 to 3.7) while a second structure nearer the symmetry plane, at $z$ about 0.0003 against the front's 0.0009, grows to 96 percent of it; at the next interval the maximum is at the second structure (x484, at $r = 0.00185$, $z = 0.00030$), and at the next it has burst to x776. The two follower-map grids and a third run on a wide fixed fine region (2048 points, no following, contrast 175, which cannot lose the front) agree at every one of these points to 0.2 to 0.6 percent through x484 and to 3 percent at x776, so the transition is a property of the solution and not of the map. The aspect ratio $z/r$ of the maximum's position drops from 0.42 to 0.16 across it, the swirl inside the maximum empties ($|u_1|$ at 0.7 of the maximum's radius, on its row, falls from 15 percent of the maximum at x395 to 3 percent at x776, and at 1.05 of the radius from 83 to 28 percent, so the structure is a ring compact in $r$), and the meridional velocity at the maximum turns from axial to radially inward ($|u^r|/|u^z|$ from 0.05 to 20 to 67). This has the sign of Hou's two-scale structure: in his Case 4 at the same viscosity (different data) a vacuum region for $u_1$ opens between the front and the axis and the growth then slows under viscous dominance \cite[Sec. 3.6]{H23b}, and in his rescaled model at dimension three the one-scale profile drifts toward two scales, which he calls a mild scaling instability \cite[Secs. 1 and 5]{H24}.

Past the transition the collapse does not resume as a one-scale law, and it does not arrest. The wide-map run and the two follower runs agree to one percent at every point through x909, and the label sequence 395, 382, 484, 776, 899, 909, 1025, 1422, 2501 carries $A\,(T - t) = 4.3$, 3.7, 4.1, 5.6, 5.4, 4.4, 3.7, 3.4, 3.0 with $T = 0.0022866$: the constant of Section~\ref{sec:consts} is replaced by pulses of about 60 percent, local fits of the exponent give a singular time bouncing between 0.0022861 and 0.0022895 over consecutive intervals, and the front and the ring alternate as the site of the maximum. No exponent is determined after x400, and those last points are on maps past their tested contrast. Followed further on a wide fixed map with ten times denser output, the label rises through 1390, 1764, 2546, 2861, 3991 and 5079, monotonically over the first fourteen of the sixteen recorded points, the vorticity maximum with it, and the structure descends onto the symmetry plane and contracts. The run passes the singular time fitted before the transition -- so that $T$ is a parameter of the one-scale regime and not a singular time of the computed solution -- with local fits of the logarithmic derivative giving a consistent later time of 0.0022867; the last two points fall back to 4337 and 4763, so the pulsing persists and the growth at the stopping point is not monotone. A twin at half the axial resolution instead peaks and decays ninefold, and a twin at twice the radial resolution reaches a third again higher amplitude at the same instant, so the decay is the coarse grid suppressing the collapse and not the collapse ending. We stop between x4000 and x6000, because the structure by then is resolved by seven cells across its width in one direction or the other on every grid we can run, against the ten-cell standard used above, and because the one cheap remedy, a tighter axial window, would take the map contrast past the value at which the mapped Poisson solve is known to fail. Two scale-invariant diagnostics are unchanged throughout that range: the circulation maximum stays pinned between 64.9 and 64.7 by its maximum principle, and the local $L^3$ norm of Section~\ref{sec:l3}, recomputed on that run, stays flat while the amplitude grows by a factor three.

\subsection{The constants}
\label{sec:consts}

Every constant in this subsection is recomputed from the archived snapshots themselves, so that each is checkable against the deposited data; where a quantity was also logged during the run we quote the recomputation. With $T = 0.0022865$, over the twelve retained states of Table~\ref{tab:states} (labels x9 to x329):
\[
A\,(T-t) = 2.62,\ 3.60,\ 3.68,\ 3.75,\ 3.81,\ 3.84,\ 3.86,\ 3.83,\ 3.83,\ 3.88,\ 3.83,\ 3.75 ,
\]
which rises out of the early transient onto a plateau near 3.85 by x72 and falls 2 percent over the last three states. The fall is not significant: it is smaller than the sensitivity to $T$ (Section~\ref{sec:fit}), and at the last instant it rests on a single map, the second map at that instant being the degraded one excluded in Section~\ref{sec:l3}. At the penultimate instant, where two independent maps both give resolved states, they agree to 0.3 percent in amplitude. What the series supports is that the amplitude constant is flat to a few percent over 1.5 units of $\log(1/(T-t))$ after the early transient, which is the Type I statement, and not a determination of its trend.

Figure~\ref{fig:4} plots the three of these that are scale-invariant. The other constants, recomputed over the same twelve instants. The collapse length
$R/\sqrt{T-t}$ reads 2.78 on the earliest state and then 2.42, 2.41, 2.39, 2.37, 2.37, 2.36, 2.38,
2.39, 2.44, 2.38, 2.31: flat to about three percent from x32 onwards, with the first state still in
the early transient. The Type I velocity constant $\sup|u|\sqrt{T-t}$ -- equivalently $\sup|u|^2(T-t)$, the Leray rate, whose divergence is what the geometric criterion of Constantin, Fefferman and Majda \cite{CFM96} makes necessary under smoothly directed vorticity -- reads 7.71, 8.89, 8.98, 9.07,
9.13, 9.19, 9.20, 9.20, 9.24, 9.70, 9.34, 9.89, a rise of eleven percent from x32 to x329 on top of
the $\pm 2$ percent grid scatter and the singular-time sensitivity of Section~\ref{sec:fit}, which is
why we do not read a growth law from it: a $\sn{1}{-7}$ change in $T$ moves it by two percent at
$T - t = \sn{2}{-6}$ and more later. The meridional Type I constant
$\sup|(u_r, u_z)|\sqrt{T-t}$ reads 6.16, 5.86, 5.79, 5.71, 5.61, 5.50, 5.38, 5.32, 5.32, 5.85, 6.23,
6.52, falling by a seventh and then recovering, with no trend over the range. And the circulation
maximum falls from 64.90 to 64.68, bounded by its maximum principle.

That the collapse length stays flat is worth one remark, because whether a collapsing core flattens as it goes is unsettled in the vortex-dynamics literature. Moffatt and Kimura argue that at large vortex Reynolds number the cores spin rapidly enough to feel an effectively axisymmetric strain and so retain a compact cross-section, flattening decreasing with $R_\Gamma$, while cautioning that curvature at the tipping points may defeat the argument \cite{MK19} -- a caution their own corrigendum then accepts, so the two are not symmetric and the question is closer to settled against the compact core than a juxtaposition would suggest; Yao and Hussain report from direct simulation the opposite, notable core flattening and stripping that increases with the Reynolds number \cite{YH20}. Our front is a strained layer in an axisymmetric collapse rather than a pair of reconnecting rings, so it is not a test of either claim; but it does not progressively flatten. $R/\sqrt{T-t}$ is flat to three percent over the range, so the cross-section settles to a fixed anisotropic shape and holds it, rather than degenerating as the collapse proceeds. That is the case in which the circulation-conserving exponent is attained with equality rather than as an inequality (Section~\ref{sec:theorems}).

The vorticity maximum, taken as the full $|\omega|$ rather than its azimuthal part, gives $|\omega|\,(T-t) = 26.7$, 61.3, 65.9, 71.3, 76.6, 82.6, 87.4, 95.3, 105.0, 146.7, 161.5, 242.5 on the same states. This rises throughout, and the last two values should not be read as a rate: past x222 the sheet tilts, the radial vorticity maximum overtaking the azimuthal one by a factor rising to 2.1 (Section~\ref{sec:front}), so the late rise in $|\omega|$ is in part the tilt and not an acceleration of the azimuthal front. Over the range where the front is untilted the growth exponent of $|\omega|$ in $1/(T-t)$ falls from 0.43 to 0.33, levelling toward the Burgers ceiling of Section~\ref{sec:front}, and the $T$-free ratio $|\omega|/A$, recomputed on the same states, reads 10.2, 17.0, 17.9, 19.0, 20.1, 21.5, 22.6, 24.9, 27.4, 37.8, 47.5, 64.7 -- rising throughout, and steeply at the end for the same reason.
